Filter hits by the slope of their trend

Source: R/filter_by.R
filter_by_slope.Rd

Refines a list of candidate hits (for example found by the statistical methods) by their trend over time. For each gene it fits a regression line of the normalized counts of its barcodes over the time points, separately in the treated and in the control samples (see compute_slope), and keeps the genes that decrease more in the treated samples than in the controls.

Usage

filter_by_slope(
  screenR_Object,
  genes,
  group_var_treatment,
  group_var_control,
  slope_control = NULL,
  slope_treatment = NULL
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

genes

The genes to filter, for example the hits found by find_gene_zscore_hit, find_camera_hit or find_roast_hit.

group_var_treatment

The values of the Treatment column of the data table (see get_sample_table) of the samples used for the treatment trend, for example the early time points and the treated samples.

group_var_control

The values of the Treatment column of the data table of the samples used for the control trend.

slope_control

An optional threshold: genes whose control slope is larger than this in absolute value are removed. Default NULL (no threshold).

slope_treatment

An optional threshold: genes whose treatment slope is smaller than this in absolute value are removed. Default NULL (no threshold).

Value

A tibble with the columns Gene, slope_control and slope_treatment, with one row for each gene that passes the filter.

Details

A gene is kept when both slopes are negative and the treatment slope is lower than the control slope, or when the control slope is zero or positive and the treatment slope negative. Before this, the optional thresholds remove the genes whose control slope is larger in absolute value than slope_control and those whose treatment slope is smaller in absolute value than slope_treatment.

See also

compute_slope, filter_by_variance, plot_trend

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))

filter_by_slope(
    screenR_Object = object, genes = c("Gene_1", "Gene_2"),
    group_var_treatment = c("T1", "T2", "TRT"),
    group_var_control = c("T1", "T2", "Time3", "Time4"),
    slope_control = 0.5, slope_treatment = 1
)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 3
#> # ℹ 3 variables: Gene <chr>, slope_control <dbl>, slope_treatment <dbl>
